A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BED-LLM, with matching authors, research objectives, and core methodology. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original 20 Questions experiments, film-preference elicitation results, and method ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, estimator-convergence analysis, longer conversations, likelihood-updating tests, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: BED-LLM retains its prior–likelihood model, hypothesis generation/filtering/retention, uniform beliefs, and explicit EIG maximization. Section 3 reorganizes the same procedure. The substantive algorithm revision in Appendix D concerns the Data–Estimation comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Animals, Celebrities, and Things with 100 targets each, plus 200 MovieLens-derived film-preference profiles. Matched and mismatched questioner–answerer settings remain. Additional model configurations and question budgets do not introduce different datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds a ReAct-style CoT comparator in Table 1 and the preference comparison in Figure 13. It also adds Data–Estimation to previously missing GPT comparisons and substantively revises that comparator's objective in Appendix D. Naive is simply renamed Prompt-Only; full Tree of Thoughts is not separately evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 adds Mistral-Large evaluations, 50-turn Qwen2.5-72B experiments, a hypothesis-sample sweep from 5 to 85, a history-conditioned likelihood control, and a runtime benchmark. The original evaluation metrics, dataset sizes, and default 20-question and five-question protocols remain.

E4.justification: New analyses examine longer-horizon performance, EIG-estimator and question-ranking sensitivity to sample count, and static versus updated likelihoods (Figures 9–10 and Table 4). Figure 7 adds a concrete GPT-4o-mini history-inconsistency case. These extend the existing ablations and retained mode-collapse example.

E5.justification: The existing benchmark standard-error convention and success-rate standard-error formula are unchanged. New Figure 10 includes shaded bands around EIG estimates without defining their statistic or reporting repetitions, leaving unclear whether uncertainty-estimation practices changed beyond the retained reporting convention.

E6.justification: Previously filled Table 1 values are retained, while v3 adds CoT, Mistral-Large, and GPT Data–Estimation results; for example, GPT-4o-mini Data–Estimation scores 64±4.8% on Animals. New figures and tables report longer-horizon results, estimator convergence, likelihood-updating outcomes, and runtimes. These are additional reports, not demonstrated improvements over v2 under unchanged procedures.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix D drops marginal hypothesis entropy as a constant. V3 explicitly derives its question-dependent mixture distribution and retains its entropy in the objective, adding corresponding estimators in Equations 6–10 and revising Algorithm 1. This substantively corrects the mathematical reasoning for Data–Estimation; BED-LLM's core EIG equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a deployment-time sequential BED framework, emphasize prior–likelihood factorization without deterministic responses, and claim improved information gathering on the same tasks. The introduction replaces a single-model numerical illustration with an aggregate performance summary without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning later-turn saturation, early stabilization of question rankings, and computational tradeoffs. Its claim that likelihood updating consistently worsens performance overstates Table 4: Animals improves from 63% to 67% for Llama-3.1-8B and from 79% to 80% for Llama-3.3-70B.

D1.justification: V3 adds explicit Prompt-Only and CoT prompts, Data–Estimation implementation details, measured runtimes, and a code-availability statement in Appendix J. Existing BED-LLM temperatures, filtering threshold, sampling budgets, and data-generation instructions are retained. The PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 adds ReAct and Tree of Thoughts references, positioning CoT and the existing Implicit Maximization comparator relative to them. The broader related-work discussion and BED-LLM's novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 renames Naive to Prompt-Only, moves belief updating before question generation in Section 3, recasts the algorithm walkthrough, and expands baseline explanations. Appendices are reorganized around new results and method descriptions, but the main section sequence and much existing prose remain.

P2.justification: V3 adds a worked method illustration, a component-comparison table, diagnostic plots, and runtime and likelihood-updating tables. Table 1 gains rows and a CoT column; the old full-results plot is reorganized into Figures 11–12. The retained mode-collapse counts are redrawn as a bar chart in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V3 improves mathematical clarity and empirical assessment through the Appendix D correction, CoT comparisons, focused diagnostics, and runtime and code information. However, Algorithm 1's unweighted pooling does not clearly implement the weighted-mixture sampling required by Equation 10, and the likelihood-updating interpretation overstates Table 4. These unresolved issues qualify the benefits and support a limited net improvement.
